title: Proximity-based column collapse and row-cluster summaries for high-density tables
creator: Ethan Ross
description: Design an interaction pattern and component refinements that reduces horizontal clutter in high-column-count virtualized tables by collapsing low-relevance columns based on cursor proximity and showing condensed row-cluster summaries. The goal is to retain discoverability and keyboard accessibility while improving perceived information density and reducing cognitive load for power users managing large result sets.
acceptance_criteria: Design spec includes proximity threshold rules, micro-interaction states (hover, focus, keyboard), and a11y keyboard flows for collapse/expand.
Figma frames: compact table, collapsed columns, expanded cluster preview, and keyboard-only flows exist and are linked in 'links'.
Prototype demonstrates smooth transition between density modes without layout jank at 1k rows and 75 columns (data mocked).
Interaction handoff file contains token mappings for spacing, focus rings, and animation durations; dev receives CSS token guidance.
Usability notes capture two edge cases: column pinned state + proximity collapse, and multi-select rows across collapsed clusters.
design_notes: Motivation: customers using Redwood Console have long, sparse tables (audit logs, embeddings indices). Traditional column-pinning and horizontal scroll reaches limits for quick scanning.

Proximity collapse idea: when the pointer/focus is centered on a column group, adjacent low-priority columns gently compress and show a collapsed pill; moving pointer to the pill expands neighboring columns.

Row-cluster summaries: adjacent rows with similar metadata (timestamp range, status) collapse into a single summary row with inline key metrics and an expand chevron. This preserves scanning while reducing vertical noise.

Density integration: this feature should be additive to existing density modes (compact / comfortable). In compact mode, proximity thresholds are smaller; in comfortable, collapse is more aggressive with richer summaries.
A11y: all collapse/expand actions must be reachable by keyboard (TAB to column header + Space to toggle), and screen reader text should announce 'collapsed columns 3 columns hidden'.
decisions: Use cursor proximity rather than scroll velocity to decide collapse to avoid accidental collapses while scrolling.
Collapsed state will render a single interactive token in the column header to minimize DOM complexity for virtualized lists.

Row-cluster summaries will be generated client-side via a light-weight clustering heuristic (time-based + status equality) with clear visual affordances and an option to disable for strict audit views.
Animations: 120ms ease-out for collapse/expand; prefer opacity + width transform where possible to avoid reflow.
review_comments: PM (Liam Ortega): Suggest adding a telemetry event for 'user-expanded-collapsed-pill' to measure discoverability.
Eng (Priya Nair): Concern about virtualization library reusing DOM nodes; recommend collapsed token be a virtualized placeholder to avoid layout thrash.
Accessibility reviewer (Jordan Blake): Request an explicit focus trap when expanding a cluster preview so keyboard users can navigate the expanded rows without losing context.
Design Lead (Rosa Kim): Approve visual style pending microcopy updates for collapsed-pill tooltip.
implementation_guidance: Keep collapsed-pill render path extremely lightweight: no nested interactive children to reduce reflow under virtualization.
Expose tokens: --table-collapse-pill-padding, --table-collapse-anim-duration, --table-cluster-bg for engineering to consume.
Provide a public Hooks API example: useProximityCollapse({ thresholdPx: 48, debounceMs: 60 }) to be used by engineering during handoff.
Fallback: when JS fails or user opts out, collapsed pills should default to expanded state so no data is hidden.
